'''Marcus Osmond Smart''' (born March 6, 1994) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Houston Rockets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Widely considered one of the most accomplished and versatile defenders of his era, <ref>{{Cite web |last=Kalbrosky |first=Bryan |title=Celtics' Marcus Smart thriving as a defender when switching onto bigs |url=https://www.hoopshype.com/story/sports/nba/celtics/2019/11/22/boston-celtics-marcus-smart-defensive-player-of-the-year/82918357007/ |access-date=2025-12-17 |website=HoopsHype |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Pavon |first=Josue |date=2020-12-15 |title=Celtics Legend: Marcus Smart Among Greatest Defenders In Franchise History |url=https://heavy.com/sports/nba/boston-celtics/marcus-smart-greatest-defenders-history/ |access-date=2025-12-17 |website=Heavy Sports |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-19 |title=Marcus Smart Becomes First Guard Since Gary Payton To Win NBA Defensive Player Of The Year - Fadeaway World |url=https://fadeawayworld.net/marcus-smart-becomes-first-guard-since-gary-payton-to-win-nba-defensive-player-of-the-year |access-date=2025-12-17 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-04-21 |title=Marcus Smart Is an Elite Defender—With or Without a DPOY Honor |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2023/04/21/celtics-marcus-smart-is-elite-defender-with-or-without-dpoy-honor |access-date=2025-12-18 |website=SI |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Rodriguez • • |first=Tristi |date=2022-05-30 |title=Kerr explains why Smart is 'the guard version' of Draymond |url=https://www.nbcsportsbayarea.com/nba/golden-state-warriors/kerr-explains-why-smart-is-the-guard-version-of-draymond/1416895/ |access-date=2025-12-18 |website=NBC Sports Bay Area & California |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-11-07 |title=The Celtics' Best Defensive Big Man Is 6-foot-3 |url=https://www.theringer.com/2019/11/07/nba/boston-celtics-marcus-smart-defense-frontcourt |access-date=2025-12-18 |website=www.theringer.com |language=en}}</ref> he has been selected to the [[NBA All-Defensive First Team]] thrice and was the [[NBA Defensive Player of the Year]] in [[2021–22 NBA season#Yearly awards|2022]], becoming only the second point guard after [[Gary Payton]] to win the award. Smart played [[college basketball]] for the [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State Cowboys]].

Smart was drafted by the [[Boston Celtics]] with the sixth overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft|2014 NBA Draft]]. He initially came off the bench for the Celtics before becoming the starting point guard in 2018. Smart helped the Celtics reach the [[NBA Finals]] in [[2022 NBA Finals|2022]]. After eight seasons in Boston, he was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]]. However, after greatly struggling with injuries in Memphis, Smart was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] in 2025. In July 2025, he signed a two-year contract with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] as a free agent, following a buyout agreement with the Wizards and subsequent clearance through waivers.

==Early life==

Marcus High School]] in Flower Mound, along with one of his future Oklahoma State teammates, Phillip Forte.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hoop Brothers: Marcus Smart, Phil Forte Share Bond Beyond Basketball |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2017/03/17/marcus-smart-phil-forte-bond-oklahoma-state-ncaa-tournament|work=si.com|last=Fischer|first=Jake |date=March 17, 2017 }}</ref> As a senior, Smart averaged 15.1 points, 9.2 rebounds, and 5.0 assists.<ref name="2011–12ESPNHS">{{cite web|title=2011-12 ESPNHS All-Americans|url=https://www.espn.com/high-school/boys-basketball/story/_/id/7811369/2011-12-espnhs-boys-basketball-all-americans|publisher=ESPN|last1=Flores|first1=Ronnie|last2=Huff|first2=Doug|access-date=April 11, 2014|date=April 17, 2012|archive-date=February 24, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140224033752/http://espn.go.com/high-school/boys-basketball/story/_/id/7811369/2011-12-espnhs-boys-basketball-all-americans|url-status=live}}</ref> In high school, Smart achieved a record of 115–6 through three seasons and was a two-time 5A state champion. He was also named a [[McDonald's All-American]] and was an ESPNHS first team All-American.<ref name="2011–12ESPNHS"/> Smart went on to set a new Team USA U18 record for steals over a five-game period when he grabbed 18 during the 2012 FIBA Americas U18 Championships in Brazil.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/sidebar/five-facts-rondo-wallace-thornton-smart-olynyk|title=Five Facts: Rondo, Wallace, Thornton, Smart, Olynyk|website=Boston Celtics|language=en|access-date=January 16, 2020|archive-date=August 12, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140812091538/http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/sidebar/five-facts-rondo-wallace-thornton-smart-olynyk|url-status=live}}</ref>

Smart played youth football until the sixth grade and continues to enjoy playing tennis in his spare time.<ref>{{cite web|title=Marcus Smart Bio|url=http://www.okstate.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=1207|work=OKState.com|access-date=March 2, 2016|archive-date=March 6, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160306183006/http://www.okstate.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=1207|url-status=live}}</ref>

Considered a five-star recruit by [[ESPN.com]], Smart was listed as the No. 1 shooting guard and the No. 10 player in the nation in 2012.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/67772/marcus-smart |title=Marcus Smart Recruiting Profile |access-date=February 26, 2015 |archive-date=February 24, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150224071142/http://espn.go.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/67772/marcus-smart |url-status=live }}</ref>

==College career==
During his freshman year at [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]], Smart led the Cowboys to a 24–8 record and they finished in third place in the Big 12 behind [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] and [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]]. He averaged 15.4 points, 5.8 rebounds, and 4.2 assists per game and led the Big 12 in steals with 99 and averaged 3.0 per game. Smart and the Cowboys earned a trip to the NCAA Tournament that year, clinching a #5 seed in the Midwest Region. During the first round of the tournament though, the Cowboys were eliminated by the #12 seed [[Oregon Ducks men's basketball|Oregon]]. On April 17, 2013, Smart held a press conference in the student union at OSU and announced that he would not declare for the NBA draft and instead return to OSU for his sophomore season.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.si.com/si-wire/2013/04/17/okla-state-marcus-smart-returning-to-school |title=Report: Okla. State's Marcus Smart to return for sophomore year |date=April 16, 2013 |access-date=December 9, 2017 |archive-date=August 1, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200801185207/https://www.si.com/si-wire/2013/04/17/okla-state-marcus-smart-returning-to-school |url-status=live }}</ref> Smart's 99 steals set a freshman record in the Big 12.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1985620-marcus-smart-player-profile-fun-facts-and-predictions-for-oklahoma-state-star|title=Marcus Smart: Player Profile, Fun Facts and Predictions for Oklahoma State Star|last=Daniels|first=Tim|website=Bleacher Report|access-date=January 16, 2020|archive-date=February 25, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220225171903/https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1985620-marcus-smart-player-profile-fun-facts-and-predictions-for-oklahoma-state-star|url-status=live}}</ref>

On November 19, 2013, Smart scored 39 points leading the #7-seed Oklahoma State Cowboys past the #11-seed [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]]. On February 8, 2014, during a game at [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]], Smart shoved a fan in the stands after a verbal altercation in the closing minutes of the game, and received a technical foul. Reports after the game stated that Smart claimed the fan yelled a racial slur at him. At a press conference the following afternoon, Smart would not comment on that element of the altercation, and coach [[Travis Ford]] chose not to address it. The fan denied using a racial slur and stated that he called Smart "a piece of crap." Audio from the incident confirmed the fan's account.<ref>{{cite web|title=Marcus Smart suspended 3 games for altercation with fan; Texas Tech releases new footage of incident|url=https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/marcus-smart-suspension-length-punishment-shove-push-fan-oklahoma-state-texas-tech-video-return-out/181xnitz87pgn1kpcyl2avql8m|work=SI.com|date=February 9, 2014|access-date=August 1, 2020|archive-date=November 11, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201111215533/https://www.sportingnews.com/us/ncaa-basketball/news/marcus-smart-suspension-length-punishment-shove-push-fan-oklahoma-state-texas-tech-video-return-out/181xnitz87pgn1kpcyl2avql8m|url-status=live}}</ref> Smart was subsequently suspended for three games and the fan agreed not to attend any further Texas Tech games during the 2013–14 season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Marcus Smart suspended 3 games for altercation with fan; Texas Tech releases new footage of incident|url=https://www.si.com/si-wire/2014/02/09/marcus-smart-suspended-3-games|work=SI.com|date=February 9, 2014|access-date=February 9, 2014|last=Maloy|first=Brendan|archive-date=November 12, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201112015612/https://www.si.com/si-wire/2014/02/09/marcus-smart-suspended-3-games|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.texastech.com/genrel/020914aab.html |title=Statement Regarding Incident At Texas Tech-Oklahoma State Men's Basketball Game |date=February 9, 2014 |access-date=February 9, 2014 |archive-date=June 30, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160630013239/http://www.texastech.com/genrel/020914aab.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Later that season, Smart was named one of the 30 finalists for the [[Naismith College Player of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web|title=2013-14 Men's Naismith Trophy Midseason 30 |url=http://www.naismithawards.com/PressBox/ArticleView/tabid/209/ArticleId/8/2013-14-Mens-Naismith-Trophy-Midseason-30.aspx |work=NaismithAwards.com |access-date=February 14, 2014 |date=February 13, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140222224557/http://www.naismithawards.com/PressBox/ArticleView/tabid/209/ArticleId/8/2013-14-Mens-Naismith-Trophy-Midseason-30.aspx |archive-date=February 22, 2014 }}</ref> In the first game of the [[2014 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2014 NCAA tournament]], the Cowboys lost to [[Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball|Gonzaga]]. Smart finished with 23 points, 13 rebounds, seven assists and six steals, becoming the first player in tournament history to record 20 points, 10 rebounds, five assists, and five steals.<ref>{{cite web|title=Marcus Smart can't get first NCAA Tournament win as his Cowboys fall to Gonzaga|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/one-and-one/2014/03/21/marcus-smart-oklahoma-state-lose-gonzaga-ncaa-tournament|work=SI.com|last=Mandel|first=Stewart|access-date=March 21, 2014|date=March 21, 2014|archive-date=April 22, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190422010020/https://www.si.com/college-basketball/one-and-one/2014/03/21/marcus-smart-oklahoma-state-lose-gonzaga-ncaa-tournament|url-status=live}}</ref>

During his two seasons at Oklahoma State, Smart averaged 16.6 points, 5.9 rebounds and 4.5 assists in 33.1 minutes per game.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/s/smartma01.html#all_all_college_stats|title=Marcus Smart Stats|website=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=November 29, 2018|archive-date=July 26, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190726232006/https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/s/smartma01.html#all_all_college_stats|url-status=live}}</ref> On April 7, 2014, he declared for the [[NBA draft]], forgoing his final two years of college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web|title=Marcus Smart entering NBA draft|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2014/story/_/id/10746052/marcus-smart-oklahoma-state-cowboys-entering-nba-draft|publisher=ESPN|access-date=April 7, 2014|date=April 7, 2014|archive-date=April 7, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140407225722/http://espn.go.com/nba/draft2014/story/_/id/10746052/marcus-smart-oklahoma-state-cowboys-entering-nba-draft|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Memphis Grizzlies (2023–2025)===
On June 22, 2023, Smart was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] as part of a three-team deal that sent [[Kristaps Porziņģis]] to the Celtics and [[Tyus Jones]] to Washington. The trade also involved the Grizzlies sending a 2023 first-round pick (pick No. 25) and a top-four-protected 2024 first-round pick (via [[Golden State Warriors]]) to the Celtics. Additionally, the [[Washington Wizards]] acquired [[Danilo Gallinari]], [[Mike Muscala]], and Boston's 2023 second-round pick (pick No. 35).<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/37896379/grizzlies-acquire-marcus-smart-celtics-3-team-deal-involving-kristaps-porzingis-tyus-jones-sources-say | title=Sources: Smart, Porzingis traded in 3-team deal | date=June 22, 2023 |access-date=June 28, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-acquire-marcus-smart-in-three-team-trade-with-boston-celtics-and-washington-wizards|title=Memphis Grizzlies acquire Marcus Smart in three-team trade with Boston Celtics and Washington Wizards|date=June 23, 2023|work=NBA.com}}</ref>

Smart played in just one game following the All-Star break, a 121–118 overtime loss to the [[Sacramento Kings]] on March 18, where he played just five minutes without recording a single stat in any category.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Marcus Smart Injuries - NBA |url=https://www.foxsports.com/nba/marcus-smart-player-injuries |access-date=2024-02-19 |website=FOX Sports |language=en-US}}</ref>

On February 6, 2025, Smart was traded to the [[Washington Wizards]] along with [[Colby Jones]] and [[Alex Len]] for [[Johnny Davis (basketball, born 2002)|Johnny Davis]], [[Marvin Bagley III]], and a 2025 second-round pick in a three-team trade that sent [[Jake LaRavia]] to the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.nba.com/wizards/news/washington-acquires-marcus-smart-colby-jones-alex-len-and-a-first-round-pick-in-multi-team-trade | title=Washington Acquires Marcus Smart, Colby Jones, Alex Len, and a First-Round Pick In Multi-Team Trade  | date=February 6, 2025 | work=NBA.com }}</ref>

On July 20, Smart was waived by the Wizards after a contract buyout agreement.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Wizards PR|title=The Washington Wizards have reached a buyout agreement with guard Marcus Smart|number=1947053922167730412|user=WizPRStats|date=July 20, 2025|access-date=July 21, 2025}}</ref>

=== Los Angeles Lakers (2025–2026) ===
On July 22, 2025, Smart signed a two-year, $11 million deal with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Los Angeles Lakers Sign Guard Marcus Smart |website=Los Angeles Lakers |url=https://lakers.com/news/los-angeles-lakers-sign-guard-marcus-smart |access-date=2025-07-22 |language=en}}</ref> [[Luka Doncic]] also played a role in recruiting Smart to the team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Luka Dončić’s Offseason Lakers Recruiting Sparked Deandre Ayton, Marcus Smart Signings |website=Yahoo Sports |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/article/luka-don-offseason-lakers-recruiting-195732950.html|language=en}}</ref>   

In December 2025, he was fined $35,000 for making an obscene gesture towards a game official at halftime during a game against the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Lakers' guard is fined for his behaviour |url=https://basketnews.com/news-237232-lakers-guard-is-fined-for-his-behaviour.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=23 December 2025 |language=en}}</ref> During Game 3 of the first round against the [[Houston Rockets]] on April 24, 2026, Smart put up what was described as a strong defensive performance, recording 21 points and 10 assists.<ref>{{Cite web |author=Dave McMenamin |date=2026-04-22 |title=Marcus Smart's breakout game helps Lakers go up 2-0 on Rockets |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/48558342/marcus-smart-helps-short-handed-lakers-win-game-2-vs-rockets |access-date=2026-04-25 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}}</ref>

=== Houston Rockets (2026–present) ===
On July 10, 2026, Smart signed a two-year, $12.4 million deal with the [[Houston Rockets]], with the second year being a player option.<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 10, 2026 |title=Rockets Sign Free Agent Marcus Smart |url=https://rockets.com/news/rockets-sign-free-agent-marcus-smart |access-date=July 10, 2026 |website=rockets.com |language=en}}</ref> This reunited him with his former [[Boston Celtics|Celtics]] head coach [[Ime Udoka]], whom he won [[NBA Defensive Player of the Year]] under in 2022.

==Player profile==
Smart plays both the point guard and shooting guard positions,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.basketballnews.com/stories/all-signs-pointing-to-marcus-smart-as-the-celtics-swing-player|title=What does Marcus Smart at point guard look like for the Celtics?|first=Ethan|last=Fuller|date=October 11, 2021|website=www.basketballnews.com}}</ref><ref name="auto1"/> but was named the Celtics' starting point guard in 2021. Standing at {{convert|6|ft|3|in}} with a {{convert|6|ft|9|in|adj=on|m}} wingspan, he is capable of guarding all five positions, enabling him to play a switching defense with historic efficiency.<ref name="auto" />

Smart has earned a reputation as a hustle player. He is known for diving for loose balls and taking charges, and has been nicknamed "the Cobra" as a result.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Story of Marcus Smart: "I Love Boston, Boston Loves Me" |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/sidebar/the-story-of-marcus-smart |access-date=2022-04-19 |website=Boston Celtics |language=en}}</ref> Due to his physicality, quick hands, and elite basketball IQ,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Polacek |first=Scott |title=Celtics' Marcus Smart Named 2021-22 NBA Defensive Player of the Year |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10033092-celtics-marcus-smart-named-2021-22-nba-defensive-player-of-the-year |access-date=2022-04-20 |work=Bleacher Report}}</ref> many consider Smart to be one of the most versatile and consistent defenders in the NBA.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2020-06-20|title=The Ringer lists Marcus Smart among NBA's 5 best on-ball defenders|url=https://celticswire.usatoday.com/2020/06/19/nba-boston-celtics-marcus-smart-5-best-on-ball-defenders/|access-date=2021-06-30|work=Celtics Wire|archive-date=July 9, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210709182514/https://celticswire.usatoday.com/2020/06/19/nba-boston-celtics-marcus-smart-5-best-on-ball-defenders/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Although not a high percentage shooter, Smart is aggressive on offense and defense. He often guards opposing players taller than him, using his physicality to make them uncomfortable and often causing turnovers or missed shots.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://fivethirtyeight.com/features/who-are-the-nbas-best-defenders-right-now/|title=Who Are The NBA's Best Defenders Right Now?|work=fivethirtyeight.com/|date=November 28, 2017|access-date=January 14, 2020|archive-date=January 14, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200114210405/https://fivethirtyeight.com/features/who-are-the-nbas-best-defenders-right-now/|url-status=dead}}</ref> Over Smart's years in the league, his three-point shooting has improved.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/marcus-smart-evolved-legitimate-3-170138070.html|title=Marcus Smart has evolved into a legitimate 3-point threat, and we have proof|work=Yahoo! Sports|date=November 12, 2019|access-date=January 14, 2020|archive-date=January 14, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200114210405/https://sports.yahoo.com/marcus-smart-evolved-legitimate-3-170138070.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Former teammate [[Kemba Walker]] describes the energy Smart brings to the game: "It's exciting. And propels our defense each and every night."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/nba/celtics-teammates-endorse-marcus-smart-for-defensive-player-of-the-year/ar-BBYINsB|title=Celtics teammates endorse Marcus Smart for Defensive Player of the Year|work=MSN Sports|date=January 6, 2020|access-date=January 14, 2020|archive-date=January 14, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200114210407/https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/nba/celtics-teammates-endorse-marcus-smart-for-defensive-player-of-the-year/ar-BBYINsB|url-status=live}}</ref>
